column2: Given joint angles q, FK multiplies the DH transform matrices in sequence to produce the end-effector pose as a 4x4 SE(3) matrix.

column1: What does the Jacobian J(q) map?
column2: Joint velocities to end-effector velocities: dx/dt = J(q) * dq/dt.

column1: Why is IK non-unique for a 6-DOF arm?
column2: Multiple joint-angle configurations (elbow-up/down, wrist-flip, etc.) produce the same end-effector pose.
A configuration where J loses rank — one or more task-space directions become uncontrollable. Detected via the smallest singular value of J.
tau = Kp * (q_des - q_act) + Kd * (dq_des - dq_act). Proportional term corrects position error; derivative term damps oscillation.

column1: How does impedance control differ from pure PD?
column2: Impedance control models the arm as a mass-spring-damper in task space, allowing compliant interaction with surfaces rather than rigid position tracking.

column1: What is MPC and at what frequency do humanoid teams run it?
column2: Model Predictive Control: at each step, solve a short-horizon trajectory optimization, execute the first action, re-plan. Humanoid balance MPC typically runs at 50-200 Hz.

column1: What is the robot dynamics equation?
column2: tau = M(q)*ddq + C(q,dq)*dq + g(q): mass matrix times acceleration plus Coriolis-centrifugal plus gravity.

column1: At what frequency does a PD controller typically run vs a VLA policy?
column2: PD controller: ~1 kHz. VLA policy: 5–30 Hz. The VLA sets targets; the PD closes the torque loop.
